prompt: Stage 4-5, level 8, 49 HP. You crafted an emblem for the trait your carry and casters share; adding one more unit of it reaches the next breakpoint. Candidate holders: the 2-star 4-cost tank (no trait overlap, permanent), the 1-star 3-cost bruiser (will be sold at 9), the 2-star support (already has the trait). Who holds it?
explanation:
An emblem is a permanent trait count, so it goes on a unit that is permanent, does not already have the trait, and has an item slot you will not need for something better. The 2-star 4-cost tank satisfies all three: it stays until the end, it has no overlap, and its third slot is worth less than the breakpoint. The support already counts for the trait, so an emblem there is a dead item. The 3-cost bruiser reaches the breakpoint too, but you will sell it for a 5-cost or a second 4-cost at level 9, and the emblem comes back to the bench mid-stage-5 when you can least afford to re-plan.

There is a subtler point: an emblem redirects what your level-9 board looks like. With the trait count locked onto the tank, every future slot is free to be the strongest unit available instead of a trait filler, which is how emblem boards cap higher than natural verticals.
principle: Emblems go on the permanent unit that does not have the trait; that frees every other slot to be pure strength.
commonMistake: Putting the emblem on the unit that is easiest to give it to now, then moving it every stage as that unit gets sold.
